229    /**
230     *  <p>{@summary Unconditionally closes an object instance of a class that implements
231     *  the interface
232     *  {@link AutoCloseable}.}</p>
233     *  <p>Equivalent to
234     *  {@link AutoCloseable#close()},
235     *  except any exceptions will be ignored. This is typically used in
236     *  {@code finally} blocks.</p>
237     *  <p>Even after the introduction of {@code try-with-resources} with
238     *  Java&nbsp;7, this method can be still helpful.</p>
239     *
240     *  @param  closeable   The {@code AutoCloseable} instance to close, can be
241     *      {@null} or already closed.
242     */
243    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
244    public static final void closeQuietly( final AutoCloseable closeable )
245    {
246        try
247        {
248            if( nonNull( closeable ) ) closeable.close();
249        }
250        catch( final Exception _ ) { /* Deliberately ignored! */ }
251    }   //  closeQuietly()

253    /**
254     *  <p>{@summary Creates a new directory by creating all nonexistent parent
255     *  directories first.} Unlike the
256     *  {@link #createDirectory(File,FileAttribute...)}
257     *  method, an exception is not thrown if the directory could not be
258     *  created because it already exists.</p>
259     *  <p>The {@code attributes} parameter is optional to set
260     *  {@linkplain FileAttribute file-attributes}
261     *  atomically when creating the non-existent directories. Each file
262     *  attribute is identified by its
263     *  {@linkplain FileAttribute#name name}.
264     *  If more than one attribute of the same name is included in the array
265     *  then all but the last occurrence is ignored.</p>
266     *  <p>If this method fails, then it may do so after creating some, but
267     *  not all, of the parent directories.</p>
268     *
269     *  @param  dir The directory to create.
270     *  @param  attributes  An optional list of file attributes to set
271     *      atomically when creating the directory.
272     *  @return The directory.
273     *  @throws UnsupportedOperationException   The attributes array contains
274     *      an attribute that cannot be set atomically when creating the
275     *      directory.
276     *  @throws java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException    The {@code dir}
277     *      exists but is not a directory <i>(optional specific exception)</i>.
278     *  @throws IOException An I/O error occurred.
279     *  @throws SecurityException   In the case a security manager is
280     *      installed, the
281     *      {@link SecurityManager#checkWrite(String) checkWrite()}
282     *      method is invoked prior to attempting to create a directory and its
283     *      {@link SecurityManager#checkRead(String) checkRead()}
284     *      is invoked for each parent directory that is checked. If
285     *      {@code dir} is not an absolute path then its
286     *      {@link File#getAbsoluteFile()}
287     *      method may need to be invoked to get its absolute path. This may
288     *      invoke the security manager's
289     *      {@link SecurityManager#checkPropertyAccess(String) checkPropertyAccess()}
290     *      method to check access to the system property {@code user.dir}.
291     *
292     *  @see Files#createDirectories(Path, FileAttribute...)
293     *  @see File#mkdirs()
294     *
295     *  @since 0.0.6
296     */
297    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.6" )
298    public static final File createDirectories( final File dir, final FileAttribute<?>... attributes ) throws IOException
299    {
300        final var path = Files.createDirectories( requireNonNullArgument( dir, "dir" ).toPath(), requireNonNullArgument( attributes, "attributes" ) );
301        final var retValue = path.toFile();
302
303        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
304        return retValue;
305    }   //  createDirectories()
306
307    /**
308     *  <p>{@summary Creates a new directory.} The check for the existence of the file and
309     *  the creation of the directory if it does not exist are a single
310     *  operation that is atomic with respect to all other filesystem
311     *  activities that might affect the directory. The
312     *  {@link #createDirectories(File, FileAttribute...) createDirectories()}
313     *  method should be used where it is required to create all nonexistent
314     *  parent directories first.</p>
315     *  <p>The {@code attributes} parameter is optional to set
316     *  {@linkplain FileAttribute file-attributes}
317     *  atomically when creating the directory. Each attribute is identified by
318     *  its
319     *  {@linkplain FileAttribute#name name}.
320     *  If more than one attribute of the same name is included in the array
321     *  then all but the last occurrence is ignored.</p>
322     *
323     *  @param  dir The directory to create.
324     *  @param  attributes  An optional list of file attributes to set
325     *      atomically when creating the directory
326     *  @return The directory.
327     *  @throws UnsupportedOperationException   The attributes array contains
328     *      an attribute that cannot be set atomically when creating the
329     *      directory.
330     *  @throws java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException    A directory could
331     *      not otherwise be created because a file of that name already exists
332     *      <i>(optional specific exception)</i>.
333     *  @throws IOException An I/O error occurred or the parent directory does
334     *      not exist.
335     *  @throws SecurityException   In the case a security manager is
336     *      installed, the
337     *      {@link SecurityManager#checkWrite(String) checkWrite()}
338     *      method is invoked to check write access to the new directory.
339     *
340     *  @since 0.0.6
341     */
342    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.6" )
343    public static File createDirectory( final File dir, final FileAttribute<?>... attributes ) throws IOException
344    {
345        final var path = Files.createDirectory( requireNonNullArgument( dir, "dir" ).toPath(), requireNonNullArgument( attributes, "attributes" ) );
346        final var retValue = path.toFile();
347
348        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
349        return retValue;
350    }   //  createDirectory()
351
352    /**
353     *  <p>{@summary Creates a directory named after the account name of the
354     *  current user (determined by the system property
355     *  {@value CommonConstants#PROPERTY_USER_NAME})
356     *  in the default {@code temp} folder, determined by the system property
357     *  {@value CommonConstants#PROPERTY_TEMPFOLDER}.}</p>
358     *  <p>The access rights are set for the current user only (for UNIX, it
359     *  would be 700).</p>
360     *  <p>The new directory will <i>not</i> be removed automatically after
361     *  program termination.</p>
362     *  <p>The class
363     *  {@link File}
364     *  provides a static method
365     *  {@link File#createTempFile(String, String) createTempFile()}
366     *  that creates a temporary file in the default temporary folder. As this
367     *  may be not a problem on a single-user Windows system with default
368     *  configuration, it will cause security problems on UNIX-like systems.
369     *  Therefore, it is recommended, to use
370     *  {@link File#createTempFile(String, String, File)}
371     *  instead, like this:</p>
372     *  <div class="source-container"><pre>final var tempFile = File.createTempFile( "PREFIX", "EXT", createTempDirectory() );</pre></div>
373     *  <p>This will guarantee that the temporary files cannot be read by
374     *  other users.</p>
375     *
376     *  @return The new temporary directory; it is guaranteed that the
377     *      directory exists after the call to this method returned.
378     *  @throws IOException Something has gone wrong.
379     *
380     *  @since 0.0.6
381     */
382    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.6" )
383    public static final File createTempDirectory() throws IOException
384    {
385        //---* Create the file object for the temp directory *-----------------
386        final var tempDir = getSystemTempFolder();
387        final var userTempDir = tempDir.resolve( getProperty( PROPERTY_USER_NAME ) );
388
389        //---* Get the file attributes *---------------------------------------
390        @SuppressWarnings( "ZeroLengthArrayAllocation" )
391        final FileAttribute<?> [] attributes = DEFAULT_FILESYSTEM_IS_POSIX_COMPLIANT ? new FileAttribute [] {PosixPermissions.tempDirPermissions} : new FileAttribute [0];
392
393        //---* Create the directory *------------------------------------------
394        final var retValue = Files.createDirectories( userTempDir, attributes ).toFile();
395
396        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
397        return retValue;
398    }   //  createTempDirectory()
399

418     *      atomically when creating the directory.

423     *  @throws UnsupportedOperationException   The attributes array contains
424     *      an attribute that cannot be set atomically when creating the

426     *  @throws IOException An I/O error occurs or {@code dir} does not exist.
427     *  @throws SecurityException   In the case a security manager is
428     *      installed, the
429     *      {@link SecurityManager#checkWrite(String) checkWrite()}

431     *      directory.
432     *

436     */
437    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.6" )
438    public static Path createTempDirectory( final File dir, final String prefix, final FileAttribute<?>... attributes ) throws IOException

440        return Files.createTempDirectory( requireNonNullArgument( dir, "dir" ).toPath(), prefix, requireNonNullArgument( attributes, "attributes" ) );

486    /**
487     *  <p>{@summary Deletes the folder (or file) that is determined by the
488     *  given
489     *  {@link Path}
490     *  instance.} If the argument denotes a directory, the method will remove
491     *  its contents first, recursively.</p>
492     *
493     *  @param  folder  The folder to remove; despite the name of the argument
494     *      and the method, this can be also a plain file.
495     *  @throws IOException A problem occurred when deleting the {@code Path}.
496     */
497    public static final void deleteFolder( final Path folder ) throws IOException
498    {
499        //noinspection AnonymousInnerClass,OverlyComplexAnonymousInnerClass
500        walkFileTree( requireNonNullArgument( folder, "folder" ), new SimpleFileVisitor<>()
501        {
502            /**
503             * {@inheritDoc}
504             */
505            @Override
506            public final FileVisitResult postVisitDirectory( final Path directory, final IOException exception ) throws IOException
507            {
508                try
509                {
510                    delete( directory );
511                }
512                catch( final IOException e )
513                {
514                    if( nonNull( exception ) ) e.addSuppressed( exception );
515                    throw e;
516                }
517
518                //---* Done *--------------------------------------------------
519                return CONTINUE;
520            }   //  postVisitDirectory()
521
522            /**
523             * {@inheritDoc}
524             */
525            @Override
526            public final FileVisitResult visitFile( final Path file, final BasicFileAttributes attributes ) throws IOException
527            {
528                delete( file );
529
530                //---* Done *--------------------------------------------------
531                return CONTINUE;
532            }   //  visitFile()
533        } );
534    }   //  deleteFolder()
535
536    /**

538     *  given
539     *  {@link File}.
540     *  instance.} If the argument denotes a directory, the method will remove
541     *  its contents first, recursively.</p>
542     *  <p>Calls

544     *  internally.</p>
545     *
546     *  @param  folder  The folder to remove; despite the name of the argument
547     *      and the method, this can be also a plain file.
548     *  @throws IOException A problem occurred when deleting the {@code Path}.
549     */
550    public static final void deleteFolder( final File folder ) throws IOException
551    {
552        deleteFolder( requireNonNullArgument( folder, "folder" ).toPath() );
553    }   //  deleteFolder()

555    /**
556     *  <p>{@summary Calculates the check sum for the given file, using the
557     *  algorithm with the given name.}</p>
558     *  <p>If the name is one of</p>
559     *  <ul>
560     *      <li>CRC32</li>
561     *      <li>Adler32</li>
562     *  </ul>
563     *  <p>the method uses
564     *  {@link java.util.zip.CRC32}
565     *  or
566     *  {@link java.util.zip.Adler32}
567     *  for the calculation, any other name is taken as the name for a
568     *  {@linkplain MessageDigest};
569     *  all JVMs know</p>
570     *  <ul>
571     *      <li>MD5</li>
572     *      <li>SHA1</li>
573     *  </ul>
574     *  <p>others can be added by installing additional
575     *  {@linkplain java.security.Provider security providers}.</p>
576     *  <p>This method calls
577     *  {@link #determineCheckSum(Path, String)}
578     *  internally.</p>
579     *
580     *  @param  file    The file to process.
581     *  @param  algorithm   The name for the algorithm to use for the check sum
582     *      calculation.
583     *  @return The check sum as a hex string.
584     *  @throws IOException Problems to process the file.
585     *  @throws NoSuchAlgorithmException    The provided algorithm does not
586     *      exist or the provider for it is not installed properly.
587     */
588    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
589    public static final String determineCheckSum( final File file, final String algorithm ) throws IOException, NoSuchAlgorithmException
590    {
591        final var retValue = determineCheckSum( requireNonNullArgument( file, "file" ).toPath(), algorithm );
592
593        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
594        return retValue;
595    }   //  determineCheckSum()
596
597    /**
598     *  <p>{@summary Calculates the check sum for the given file, using the
599     *  algorithm with the given name.}</p>
600     *  <p>If the name is one of</p>
601     *  <ul>
602     *      <li>CRC32</li>
603     *      <li>Adler32</li>
604     *  </ul>
605     *  <p>the method uses
606     *  {@link java.util.zip.CRC32}
607     *  or
608     *  {@link java.util.zip.Adler32}
609     *  for the calculation, any other name is taken as the name for a
610     *  {@linkplain MessageDigest};
611     *  all JVMs know</p>
612     *  <ul>
613     *      <li>MD5</li>
614     *      <li>SHA1</li>
615     *  </ul>
616     *  <p>others can be added by installing additional
617     *  {@linkplain java.security.Provider security providers}.</p>
618     *
619     *  @param  file    The file to process.
620     *  @param  algorithm   The name for the algorithm to use for the check sum
621     *      calculation.
622     *  @return The check sum as a hex string.
623     *  @throws IOException Problems to process the file.
624     *  @throws NoSuchAlgorithmException    The provided algorithm does not
625     *      exist or the provider for it is not installed properly.
626     */
627    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
628    public static final String determineCheckSum( final Path file, final String algorithm ) throws IOException, NoSuchAlgorithmException
629    {
630        final var retValue = switch( requireNotEmptyArgument( algorithm, "algorithm" ) )
631        {
632            case "Adler32" -> Hash.create( file, new Adler32() ).toString();
633            case "CRC32" -> Hash.create( file, new CRC32() ).toString();
634            default -> Hash.create( file, MessageDigest.getInstance( algorithm ) ).toString();
635        };
636
637        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
638        return retValue;
639    }   //  determineCheckSum()
640
641    /**
642     *  Calculates the check sum for the given file, using provided check sum
643     *  algorithm implementation.

645     *  @param  file    The file to process.
646     *  @param  algorithm   The check sum algorithm to use for the check sum
647     *      calculation.
648     *  @return The check sum.
649     *  @throws IOException Problems to process the file.
650     */
651    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
652    public static final long determineCheckSum( final File file, final Checksum algorithm ) throws IOException
653    {
654        final var retValue = determineCheckSum( requireNonNullArgument( file, "file" ).toPath(), algorithm );
655
656        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
657        return retValue;

674            .number()

677        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------

747    /**
748     *  <p>{@summary Returns a
749     *  {@link PathMatcher}
750     *  for the
751     *  {@linkplain FileSystems#getDefault() default filesystem}
752     *  that performs match operations on the String representation of
753     *  {@link Path}
754     *  objects by interpreting a given pattern.}</p>
755     *  <p>The {@code syntaxAndPattern} parameter identifies the syntax and the
756     *  pattern and takes the form:</p>
757     *  <blockquote><pre>
758     *  [<i>syntax</i><b>:</b>]<i>pattern</i>
759     *  </pre></blockquote>
760     *  <p>where <i>syntax</i> is the non-empty name of the syntax, <i>pattern</i>
761     *  is a possibly-empty pattern string, and {@code ':'} stands for
762     *  itself.</p>
763     *  <p>A
764     *  {@link java.nio.file.FileSystem FileSystem}
765     *  implementation supports the &quot;{@code glob}&quot; and
766     *  &quot;{@code regex}&quot; syntaxes, and may support others. The value
767     *  of the syntax component is compared without regard to case. If no
768     *  syntax is provided explicitly, &quot;{@code glob}&quot; is assumed.</p>
769     *  <p>When the syntax is &quot;{@code glob}&quot; then the {@code String}
770     *  representation of the path is matched using a limited pattern language
771     *  that resembles regular expressions but with a simpler syntax. For
772     *  example:</p>
773     *  <table class="striped"
774     *         style="text-align:left; margin-left:2em">
775     *      <caption style="display:none">Pattern Language</caption>
776     *      <thead>
777     *          <tr>
778     *              <th scope="col">Example</th>
779     *              <th scope="col">Description</th>
780     *          </tr>
781     *      </thead>
782     *      <tbody>
783     *          <tr>
784     *              <th scope="row">{@code *.java}</th>
785     *              <td>Matches a path that represents a file name ending in
786     *              {@code .java}</td>
787     *          </tr>
788     *          <tr>
789     *              <th scope="row">{@code *.*}</th>
790     *              <td>Matches file names containing a dot</td>
791     *          </tr>
792     *          <tr>
793     *              <th scope="row">{@code *.{java,class}}</th>
794     *              <td>Matches file names ending with {@code .java} or
795     *              {@code .class}</td>
796     *          </tr>
797     *          <tr>
798     *              <th scope="row">{@code foo.?}</th>
799     *              <td>Matches file names starting with {@code foo.} and a
800     *              single character extension</td>
801     *          </tr>
802     *          <tr>
803     *              <th scope="row"><code>&#47;home&#47;*&#47;*</code>
804     *              <td>Matches <code>&#47;home&#47;gus&#47;data</code> on
805     *              UNIX platforms</td>
806     *          </tr>
807     *          <tr>
808     *              <th scope="row"><code>&#47;home&#47;**</code>
809     *              <td>Matches <code>&#47;home&#47;gus</code> and
810     *              <code>&#47;home&#47;gus&#47;data</code> on UNIX
811     *              platforms</td>
812     *          </tr>
813     *          <tr>
814     *              <th scope="row"><code>C:&#92;&#92;*</code>
815     *              <td>Matches <code>C:&#92;foo</code> and
816     *              <code>C:&#92;bar</code> on the Windows platform (note that
817     *              the backslash is escaped; as a string literal in the Java
818     *              Language the pattern would be
819     *              <code>"C:&#92;&#92;&#92;&#92;*"</code>)</td>
820     *          </tr>
821     *      </tbody>
822     *  </table>
823     *  <p>The following rules are used to interpret glob patterns:</p>
824     *  <ul>
825     *      <li><p>The {@code *} character matches zero or more
826     *      {@link Character characters}
827     *      of a
828     *      {@link Path#getName(int) name}
829     *      component without crossing directory boundaries.</p></li>
830     *      <li><p>The {@code **} characters matches zero or more
831     *      {@link Character characters}
832     *      crossing directory boundaries.</p></li>
833     *      <li><p>The {@code ?} character matches exactly one character of a
834     *      name component.</p></li>
835     *      <li><p>The backslash character ({@code \}) is used to escape
836     *      characters that would otherwise be interpreted as special
837     *      characters. The expression &quot;{@code \\}&quot; matches a single
838     *      backslash and &quot;<code>\{</code>&quot; matches a left brace for
839     *      example.</p></li>
840     *      <li><p>The {@code [ ]} characters are a <i>bracket expression</i>
841     *      that match a single character of a name component out of a set of
842     *      characters.</p>
843     *      <p>For example, {@code [abc]} matches {@code "a"}, {@code "b"},
844     *      or {@code "c"}.</p>
845     *      <p>The hyphen ({@code -}) may be used to specify a range so
846     *      {@code [a-z]} specifies a range that matches from {@code "a"} to
847     *      {@code "z"} (inclusive).</p>
848     *      <p>These forms can be mixed so [abce-g] matches {@code "a"}, {@code "b"},
849     *      {@code "c"}, {@code "e"}, {@code "f"} or {@code "g"}. If the
850     *      character after the {@code [} is a {@code !} then it is used for
851     *      negation so {@code [!a-c]} matches any character <i>except</i>
852     *      {@code "a"}, {@code "b"}, or {@code "c"}.</p>
853     *      <p>Within a bracket expression the {@code *}, {@code ?} and
854     *      {@code \} characters match themselves. The ({@code -}) character
855     *      matches itself if it is the first character within the brackets, or
856     *      the first character after the {@code !} if negating.</p></li>
857     *      <li><p>The {@code { }} characters are a group of subpatterns, where
858     *      the group matches if any subpattern in the group matches. The
859     *      {@code ","} character is used to separate the subpatterns. Groups
860     *      cannot be nested.</p></li>
861     *      <li><p> Leading period<code>&#47;</code>dot characters in file name
862     *      are treated as regular characters in match operations. For example,
863     *      the {@code "*"} glob pattern matches file name {@code ".login"}.
864     *      The
865     *      {@link Files#isHidden}
866     *      method may be used to test whether a file is considered
867     *      hidden.</p></li>
868     *      <li><p>All other characters match themselves in an implementation
869     *      dependent manner. This includes characters representing any
870     *      {@linkplain java.nio.file.FileSystem#getSeparator name-separators}.</p></li>
871     *      <li><p>How
872     *      {@link Path#getRoot root}
873     *      components are matching is highly implementation-dependent and is
874     *      not specified.</p></li>
875     *  </ul>
876     *  <p>When the syntax is "{@code regex}" then the pattern component is a
877     *  regular expression as defined by the
878     *  {@link java.util.regex.Pattern}
879     *  class.</p>
880     *  <p>For both the {@code glob} and {@code regex} syntaxes, the matching
881     *  details, such as whether the matching is case-sensitive, are
882     *  implementation-dependent and therefore not specified.</p>
883     *
884     *  @param  syntaxAndPattern    The syntax and pattern.
885     *  @return A path matcher that may be used to match paths against the
886     *      pattern.
887     *  @throws PatternSyntaxException  The given pattern is invalid.
888     *  @throws UnsupportedOperationException   The pattern syntax is not known
889     *      to the implementation.
890     *
891     *  @see Files#newDirectoryStream(Path,String)
892     *
893     *  @since 0.25.3
894     */
895    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.25.3" )
896    public static final PathMatcher getPathMatcher( final CharSequence syntaxAndPattern )
897    {
898        final var parts = splitString( requireNonNullArgument( syntaxAndPattern, "syntaxAndPattern" ), ':' );
899        final var fileSystem = FileSystems.getDefault();
900        final var effectiveSyntaxAndPattern = new StringJoiner( ":" );
901        if( parts.length == 1 ) effectiveSyntaxAndPattern.add( "glob" );
902        for( final var p : parts ) effectiveSyntaxAndPattern.add( p );
903        final var retValue = fileSystem.getPathMatcher( effectiveSyntaxAndPattern.toString() );
904
905        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
906        return retValue;
907    }   //  getPathMatcher()
908
909    /**
910     *  <p>{@summary Returns
911     *  {@link System#out}
912     *  with a non-functional
913     *  {@link OutputStream#close()}
914     *  method.}</p>
915     *  <p>Assume the following scenario:</p>
916     *  <div class="source-container"><pre>&hellip;
917     *  Optional&lt;File&gt; outputFile = &hellip;
918     *  &hellip;
919     *  PrintStream outputStream = outputFile.isPresent() ? new PrintStream( new FileOutputStream( outputFile.get() ) ) : IOUtils.getUncloseableOut();
920     *  try( outputStream )
921     *  {
922     *      &#47;**
923     *       * Print something ...
924     *       *&#47;
925     *       &hellip;
926     *  }
927     *  &hellip;</pre></div>
928     *  <p>The output stream will be close at the end of the {@code try} block;
929     *  this is desired in case of a
930     *  {@link java.io.FileOutputStream FileOutputStream},
931     *  but totally not wanted if the output stream is {@code System.out}.</p>
932     *
933     *  @return {@code System.out} without the {@code close()} method.
934     */
935    @SuppressWarnings( "ImplicitDefaultCharsetUsage" )
936    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.7" )
937    public static final PrintStream getUncloseableOut()
938    {
939        @SuppressWarnings( {"AnonymousInnerClass", "UseOfSystemOutOrSystemErr"} )
940        final var retValue = new PrintStream( out )
941        {
942            /**
943             *  {@inheritDoc}
944             */
945            @Override
946            public final void close() { /* Does nothing */ }
947        };
948
949        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
950        return retValue;
951    }   //  getUncloseableOut()
952
953    /**
954     *  <p>{@summary Reads the complete content of the provided
955     *  {@link Reader}
956     *  into a
957     *  {@link String}.}</p>
958     *  <p>Obviously this method is feasible only for files with a limited
959     *  size.</p>
960     *
961     *  @param  reader  The {@code Reader} instance.
962     *  @return The content of the provided {@code Reader}.
963     *  @throws IOException Problems on reading from the {@code Reader}.
964     */
965    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
966    public static final String loadToString( final Reader reader ) throws IOException
967    {
968        final var builder = new StringBuilder( DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE );
969        final var buffer = new char [DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE];
970        var bytesRead = requireNonNullArgument( reader, "reader" ).read( buffer );
971        while( bytesRead > 0 )
972        {
973            builder.append( buffer, 0, bytesRead );
974            bytesRead = reader.read( buffer );
975        }
976        final var retValue = builder.toString();
977
978        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
979        return retValue;
980    }   //  loadToString()
981
982    /**
983     *  <p>{@summary Parses a list of file name patterns to a list of
984     *  {@link PathMatcher}
985     *  instances.}</p>
986     *  <p>The syntax for the patterns is described in the documentation for
987     *  {@link #getPathMatcher(CharSequence) getPathMatcher()}.</p>
988     *
989     *  @param  patterns    The list of patterns.
990     *  @return  The unmodifiable list of
991     *      {@link PathMatcher}
992     *      instances.
993     */
994    public static final Collection<PathMatcher> parseFilePatterns( final CharSequence... patterns )
995    {
996        final var retValue = parseFilePatterns( asList( requireNonNullArgument( patterns, "patterns" ) ) );
997
998        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
999        return retValue;
1000    }   //  parseFilePatterns()
1001
1002    /**
1003     *  <p>{@summary Parses a list of file name patterns to a list of
1004     *  {@link PathMatcher}
1005     *  instances.}</p>
1006     *  <p>The syntax for the patterns is described in the documentation for
1007     *  {@link #getPathMatcher(CharSequence) getPathMatcher()}.</p>
1008     *
1009     *  @param  patterns    The list of patterns.
1010     *  @return  The unmodifiable list of
1011     *      {@link PathMatcher}
1012     *      instances.
1013     */
1014    public static final Collection<PathMatcher> parseFilePatterns( final Collection<? extends CharSequence> patterns )
1015    {
1016        final Collection<PathMatcher> buffer = new ArrayList<>();
1017        for( final var pattern : requireNonNullArgument( patterns, "patterns" ) )
1018        {
1019            if( isNull( pattern ) ) throw new IllegalArgumentException( "A pattern is null" );
1020            try
1021            {
1022                final var matcher = getPathMatcher( pattern.toString() );
1023                buffer.add( matcher );
1024            }
1025            catch( final PatternSyntaxException | UnsupportedOperationException e )
1026            {
1027                throw new IllegalArgumentException( "Invalid Pattern: %s".formatted( pattern ), e );
1028            }
1029        }
1030
1031        final var retValue = List.copyOf( buffer );
1032
1033        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1034        return retValue;
1035    }   //  parseFilePatterns()
1036}
